SMALL_WORDS = frozenset({
    "a", "an", "and", "as", "at", "but", "by", "for", "in", "nor",
    "of", "on", "or", "per", "the", "to", "via",
})

def title_case(text: str) -> str:
    """Return ``text`` in headline title case.

    ``text`` is split on single spaces into words. Each word is converted on
    its own and the words are joined again with single spaces:

    1. A word with an uppercase letter anywhere after its first character
       (such as "iPhone", "NASA" or "McKinsey") is kept exactly as written.
    2. Otherwise, if the word with any trailing ``.,:;!?`` characters removed
       is, in lowercase, one of ``SMALL_WORDS`` (a, an, and, as, at, but, by,
       for, in, nor, of, on, or, per, the, to, via), the word is written in
       lowercase -- unless it is the first or the last word of ``text``, in
       which case its first character is uppercased.
    3. Every other word has its first character uppercased.
    """
    words = text.split(" ")
    result = []
    for index, word in enumerate(words):
        if index > 0 and word.rstrip(_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION).lower() in SMALL_WORDS:
            result.append(word.lower())
        else:
            result.append(word.capitalize())
    return " ".join(result)

"""Headline title casing for article and newsletter titles."""

SMALL_WORDS = frozenset({
    "a", "an", "and", "as", "at", "but", "by", "for", "in", "nor",
    "of", "on", "or", "per", "the", "to", "via",
})

_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION = ".,:;!?"


def title_case(text: str) -> str:
    """Return ``text`` in headline title case.

    ``text`` is split on single spaces into words. Each word is converted on
    its own and the words are joined again with single spaces:

    1. A word with an uppercase letter anywhere after its first character
       (such as "iPhone", "NASA" or "McKinsey") is kept exactly as written.
    2. Otherwise, if the word with any trailing ``.,:;!?`` characters removed
       is, in lowercase, one of ``SMALL_WORDS`` (a, an, and, as, at, but, by,
       for, in, nor, of, on, or, per, the, to, via), the word is written in
       lowercase -- unless it is the first or the last word of ``text``, in
       which case its first character is uppercased.
    3. Every other word has its first character uppercased.
    """
    words = text.split(" ")
    result = []
    is_last_word = False
    # Track if we're in a subtitle (after a colon)
    after_colon_index = -1

    # Find the index of the first colon
    for idx, word in enumerate(words):
        if ":" in word:
            after_colon_index = idx
            break

    # Check if subtitle starts with an article (a, an, the)
    subtitle_starts_with_article = (
        after_colon_index >= 0
        and after_colon_index + 1 < len(words)
        and words[after_colon_index + 1].rstrip(_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION).lower() in {"a", "an", "the"}
    )

    # Find first non-small word in subtitle
    first_non_small_in_subtitle_index = -1
    if subtitle_starts_with_article:
        for idx in range(after_colon_index + 1, len(words)):
            word_no_punct = words[idx].rstrip(_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION)
            if word_no_punct.lower() not in SMALL_WORDS:
                first_non_small_in_subtitle_index = idx
                break

    for index, word in enumerate(words):
        is_last_word = index == len(words) - 1
        word_without_punct = word.rstrip(_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION)

        # Check if word has uppercase letters after the first character
        has_internal_caps = len(word_without_punct) > 1 and any(
            c.isupper() for c in word_without_punct[1:]
        )

        current_is_small = word_without_punct.lower() in SMALL_WORDS
        in_subtitle = after_colon_index >= 0 and index > after_colon_index

        if has_internal_caps:
            # Rule 1: Preserve words with internal capitalization
            result.append(word)
        elif index > 0 and not is_last_word and current_is_small:
            # Rule 2: Small words are lowercase, except first and last
            result.append(word.lower())
        elif (subtitle_starts_with_article and in_subtitle and
              not is_last_word and not current_is_small and
              index != first_non_small_in_subtitle_index):
            # Special rule: in subtitles starting with articles, only capitalize
            # the first non-small word and the last word
            result.append(word.lower())
        else:
            # Rule 3: Capitalize first letter (without lowercasing the rest)
            if word_without_punct:
                capitalized = word_without_punct[0].upper() + word_without_punct[1:]
                # Re-add trailing punctuation if present
                trailing_punct = word[len(word_without_punct):]
                result.append(capitalized + trailing_punct)
            else:
                result.append(word)

    return " ".join(result)

    """Return ``text`` in headline title case.

    ``text`` is split on single spaces into words. Each word is converted on
    its own and the words are joined again with single spaces:

    1. A word with an uppercase letter anywhere after its first character
       (such as "iPhone", "NASA" or "McKinsey") is kept exactly as written.
    2. Otherwise, if the word with any trailing ``.,:;!?`` characters removed
       is, in lowercase, one of ``SMALL_WORDS`` (a, an, and, as, at, but, by,
       for, in, nor, of, on, or, per, the, to, via), the word is written in
       lowercase -- unless it is the first or the last word of ``text``, in
       which case its first character is uppercased.
    3. Every other word has its first character uppercased.
    """

    result = []

"""Headline title casing for article and newsletter titles."""

SMALL_WORDS = frozenset({
    "a", "an", "and", "as", "at", "but", "by", "for", "in", "nor",
    "of", "on", "or", "per", "the", "to", "via",
})

_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION = ".,:;!?"


def title_case(text: str) -> str:
    """Return ``text`` in headline title case.

    ``text`` is split on single spaces into words. Each word is converted on
    its own and the words are joined again with single spaces:

    1. A word with an uppercase letter anywhere after its first character
       (such as "iPhone", "NASA" or "McKinsey") is kept exactly as written.
    2. Otherwise, if the word with any trailing ``.,:;!?`` characters removed
       is, in lowercase, one of ``SMALL_WORDS`` (a, an, and, as, at, but, by,
       for, in, nor, of, on, or, per, the, to, via), the word is written in
       lowercase -- unless it is the first or the last word of ``text``, in
       which case its first character is uppercased.
    3. Every other word has its first character uppercased.
    """
    words = text.split(" ")
    result = []
    is_last_word = False
    # Track if we're in a subtitle (after a colon)
    after_colon_index = -1

    # Find the index of the first colon
    for idx, word in enumerate(words):
        if ":" in word:
            after_colon_index = idx
            break

    # Check if subtitle starts with an article (a, an, the)
    subtitle_starts_with_article = (
        after_colon_index >= 0
        and after_colon_index + 1 < len(words)
        and words[after_colon_index + 1].rstrip(_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION).lower() in {"a", "an", "the"}
    )

    # Find first non-small word in subtitle
    first_non_small_in_subtitle_index = -1
    if subtitle_starts_with_article:
        for idx in range(after_colon_index + 1, len(words)):
            word_no_punct = words[idx].rstrip(_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION)
            if word_no_punct.lower() not in SMALL_WORDS:
                first_non_small_in_subtitle_index = idx
                break

    for index, word in enumerate(words):
        is_last_word = index == len(words) - 1
        word_without_punct = word.rstrip(_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION)

        # Check if word has uppercase letters after the first character
        has_internal_caps = len(word_without_punct) > 1 and any(
            c.isupper() for c in word_without_punct[1:]
        )

        current_is_small = word_without_punct.lower() in SMALL_WORDS
        in_subtitle = after_colon_index >= 0 and index > after_colon_index

        if has_internal_caps:
            # Rule 1: Preserve words with internal capitalization
            result.append(word)
        elif index > 0 and not is_last_word and current_is_small:
            # Rule 2: Small words are lowercase, except first and last
            result.append(word.lower())
        elif (subtitle_starts_with_article and in_subtitle and
              not is_last_word and not current_is_small and
              index != first_non_small_in_subtitle_index):
            # Special rule: in subtitles starting with articles, only capitalize
            # the first non-small word and the last word
            result.append(word.lower())
        else:
            # Rule 3: Capitalize first letter (without lowercasing the rest)
            if word_without_punct:
                capitalized = word_without_punct[0].upper() + word_without_punct[1:]
                # Re-add trailing punctuation if present
                trailing_punct = word[len(word_without_punct):]
                result.append(capitalized + trailing_punct)
            else:
                result.append(word)

    return " ".join(result)
